blocks.caption: Terms of use, online threats and defences (original diagram after topics 7.1 and 7.2).
blocks.long_description: Terms of use set out what users must do, limit the provider's liability, explain how data are used, protect the provider's intellectual property and say when an account can be closed; users keep rights to privacy, information and withdrawing consent. Spam floods you with unwanted offers and is stopped by spam filters; spyware secretly watches you and is caught by antivirus software; cookies remember logins but can track you, so manage them; phishing sends fake messages that pretend to be your bank, so check the sender and do not click links; pharming sends you to a fake copy of a real site, so check the address, https and the padlock.

blocks.prompt: Which is NOT a common clause (MCQ 1)? What does a limitation-of-liability clause do (MCQ 2)?
blocks.explanation: (c) product advertising; (b) it limits the company's liability if things go wrong.

blocks.prompt: Explain the common clauses and how they protect both provider and user (long question 1).
blocks.explanation: User obligations protect the provider and other users by forbidding misuse, and tell users what is expected. Limitation of liability protects the provider from unreasonable claims for outages, while telling users what risk they carry. Privacy and data use protect users by stating how their data are handled. Intellectual property protects the provider's content and tells users what they may not copy. Termination of service protects the community by allowing harmful accounts to be closed, and tells users the rules that can cost them access. Clear clauses help both sides avoid disputes.

items: Five clauses: obligations, liability limits, privacy, intellectual property, termination.
